concepts.name: Window Invariant & Two-Pointer Mental Model
concepts.mental_model: An inchworm crawling along a branch: its front foot (R) reaches forward one leaf at a time; its back foot (L) only lifts and catches up when the stretch between them breaks the rule. The worm's body is always one contiguous stretch of branch — it never teleports to a leaf further down.
concepts.mnemonic: An inchworm can't skip a leaf — sliding window only ever crawls (contiguous), never jumps (no subsequences).

past_mistakes.note: First teach-back described the expand/shrink mechanics correctly but omitted WHY it's O(n) — didn't connect 'L and R only move forward' to the 2n bound on total work.

Claimed removing the post-loop 'max_len = max(...)' line would break the last-character case, on the theory the loop exits before the last char is processed. Actually the loop body updates max_len for right = len(s)-1 BEFORE right increments past it — the last character's window is always scored inside the loop.

On LC-3090 ('at most 2 occurrences of each char'), first attempt used a plain set (presence-only) plus one shared global 'k=2' budget spent across the whole string, instead of a per-character frequency map. Self-corrected to defaultdict(int) + shrink-while-count>2 once the misconception ('k is a global one-time pass, not per-character') was named. Lesson: reach for a frequency map, not a set, whenever the rule is 'how many times', not just 'has this been seen'.

concepts.name: Fixed-Size Window
concepts.mental_model: A rigid train car exactly k seats long, rolling forward one seat at a time: one passenger boards the front, one gets bumped off the back, every single slide. Unlike the inchworm (topic 1), it never stretches or shrinks.
concepts.mnemonic: Same R twice: add nums[R], drop nums[R-k]. Both use the NEW right index, never the old one.

past_mistakes.note: Pretest: described the outgoing index as 'i-k' using the OLD right edge i, instead of using the NEW right edge after sliding (correct: (i+1)-k). Classic off-by-one — pretest, not recorded as a miss, but the exact gap this topic's mnemonic targets.

On LC-643, first cut used integer division (curr_sum // k) instead of true division, truncating the average. Self-corrected to '/'. Also initialized max_avg = 0, which silently breaks on all-negative input (a valid LC-643 case) since 0 beats any real negative average. Self-corrected to float('-inf') immediately once asked. General lesson: any 'track the max' accumulator needs -inf as its floor, not 0, unless 0 is provably always achievable.

concepts.name: Variable-Size Window (Shrinkable)
concepts.mental_model: The code skeleton IS the model: `state += arr[right]` runs every step, unconditionally; then `while is_valid(state):` alternates recording the current window and removing arr[left]. Record always comes before remove, because [left,right] is only still valid before that removal.
concepts.mnemonic: A-R-R: Add (once, no condition) → while valid: Record, Remove, repeat. The while loop has no idea whether an answer is 'good' — it only stops when is_valid(state) turns False. That's the entire stopping rule.

past_mistakes.note: Pretest: first instinct was 'keep expanding since the condition (sum >= target) is satisfied,' missing that for a MINIMUM-length objective, expanding can only ever grow the window — shrinking while still valid is what searches for something smaller. Self-corrected on the follow-up question before any teaching happened.
